title: Volume measurement and biophysical characterization of mounds in epithelial monolayers after intracellular bacterial infection
protocol: Mix 1:100 collagen I solution in PBS.
Add 500 μL of collagen I solution to each well of the multi-well plate.
Incubate for 30 min at 37°C.
Aspirate out the media from the MDCK cell flask.
Wash the cell surface with 10 mL PBS once.
Add 2 mL of 0.25% trypsin/EDTA to the cells.
Place the flask in the incubator at 37°C for 10 min or until all cells detach.
Add 8 mL of complete DMEM media to the cells.
Count the number of cells per mL using a hemocytometer.
Prepare a solution of 2×10^5 cells/mL.
Concentrate cells by centrifugation or dilute as appropriate to obtain the correct concentration.
Remove the multi-well plate from the incubator.
Aspirate the collagen solution from the wells.
Wash the wells with PBS once.
Add 1 mL of cell solution in each well.
Let MDCK cells attach and proliferate for 24 hours prior to infection.
On the day of infection, estimate the concentration of cells per well to be double what was seeded (i.e., 4×10^5 cells/well).
By that point, the cells should have formed a confluent monolayer.
Add 2 mL of liquid BHI and the appropriate antibiotic in a 15 mL falcon tube.
Using a sterile pipette tip, select a single colony from the BHI agar plate and drop it into the liquid.
Loosely screw on the cover of the tube.
Place the tubes in dark without agitation.
Let the culture grow for 16–18 hours at 25°C.
Prior to infection, measure the concentration of bacteria using a spectrophotometer.
Dilute the bacterial solution 1:2 in BHI and place it in a disposable cuvette.
Measure the optical density (OD) at λ= 600 nm.
If OD600 is lower than 0.8, let the bacteria grow for a longer time.
If OD600 is slightly higher than 0.8 prior to infection, dilute appropriately.
Concentrate 2 mL of bacterial suspension by centrifugation at 2000 × g for 4 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the bacterial pellet in 2 mL of tissue culture PBS.
Wash the bacteria twice more by centrifugation as above and resuspend in 2 mL PBS.
Prepare the infection mix by mixing the bacterial-PBS suspension with complete DMEM media at a ratio of 1:16 (1 mL bacterial suspension and 15 mL of DMEM media).
Remove the culture media from the wells.
Wash cells with 1 mL media.
Add 1 mL of bacterial mix to each well.
Cover the plate with its lid and place the plates in the incubator for 30 min.
Wash the samples 4 times with media.
Replace the media in the wells with fresh DMEM media supplemented with 20 μg/mL gentamicin.
Plate 100 μL of the bacterial solution used for infection at different dilutions (1:10^2, 1:10^3, 1:10^4, 1:10^5) on BHI agar plates with appropriate antibiotics.
Use a bacterial spreader or beads to ensure that bacteria are homogeneously spread on the plates.
After 48 hours, count the number of colonies formed in the higher dilution plates (i.e., 1: 104 and 1: 105).
Average out the colony counts to calculate the resulting MOI.
Calculate MOI using the formula:
( Number of colonies · Dilution factor / Volume of bacterial solution on agar plates ) · Volume of bacterial solution added to host cells / Number of host cells
Observe single infection foci by epifluorescence microscopy starting 4–5 hpi.
Measure large domains (>300 μm) of uninfected cells surrounding infection foci.
Monitor the formation of infection mounds comprised of hundreds of squeezed and/or extruded infected cells at about 16 hpi.
Acquire 3D confocal microscopy images to characterize the resulting volume of infection mounds at 24 hpi.
Process acquired image data to calculate the volume of infection mounds.
Incubate the samples for 10 min at 37°C with 1 μg/mL Hoechst in culture media to stain the host cells’ nuclei.
Wash the samples once gently with 1 mL PBS.
Fix the samples for 10 min at 25°C in pre-warmed (37°C) freshly-made 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS.
Wash the samples with PBS twice.
Store samples at 4°C for future imaging.
Place the multi-well plate on the appropriate stage insert on the confocal microscope stage.
Choose rapid spinning disk confocal microscopy over laser-scanning confocal microscopy due to the number of images needed.
Use a 60× 1.4NA Plan Apo oil objective given the size of infection mounds.
Locate the focal plane where the cell monolayer is situated.
Identify a single infection focus using bacterial fluorescence.
Acquire confocal images of Hoechst-stained host cell nuclei.
Use a z spacing of 0.2 μm for MDCK cells.
Select one field of view centered on the infection mound for MDCK cells.
Adjust z spacing to 0.7 μm for A431D cells.
Acquire nine fields of view and stitch them together for A431D cells.
Process images using custom-built MATLAB scripts.
Extract volume data from confocal images.
Crop out lower z slices corresponding to cells still attached to the substratum for volume quantification.
Acquire confocal slices for uninfected cells.
Crop out the lower z slices that refer to cells still attaching on their substratum.
Subtract a background image of a dummy coverslip lacking cells from the image of the host cell nuclei.
Correct for uneven illumination by dividing the nucleus channel by a flatfield image acquired using a concentrated dye slide.
Add 5 μL of 50 mg/mL coumarin dye to a Micro90-cleaned slide.
Add a coverslip onto the slide and seal with nail polish.
Find the focal plane using a confocal microscope.
Obtain a z stack of images at multiple positions that extend well above and below the focal plane.
Divert light to the eyepiece.
Capture 100 images in a time series using the same intensity and exposure settings as chosen for the flatfield image.
Perform a median projection to convert the stack into one dark image.
Apply a median filter to every slice of the flatfield image.
Make a maximum intensity projection.
Subtract the dark image from the flatfield image at each position.
Perform a median projection across positions to obtain one flatfield image.
Divide by a uniform matrix of similar intensity to the flatfield image if applying a flatfield correction produces artifacts.
Correct for the difference in intensity between the flatfield and nucleus images.
Convert the grayscale into a binary image by applying an appropriate threshold.
Check the binary mask against the grayscale nucleus image at intervals of 10 z-slices.
Adjust the value of the threshold if necessary.
Add up the area of each z slice after converting the area into μm².
Multiply by the increment between each z slice to obtain the volume of the mound in μm³.
Supplement Leibovitz’s L-15 with 10% FBS and 20 μg/mL gentamicin and warm to 37°C.
Replace the DMEM-based existing medium in which host cells are immersed with 1 mL of live-microscopy medium at approximately 24 hpi.
Transfer multi-well plate onto the stage of a confocal microscope equilibrated to 37°C when mounds are readily visible at 24 hpi.
Locate an infection focus and decide what type of wound you will create.
Decide the orientation of the wound: vertically, horizontally, or around the mound.
Start acquiring confocal images of the E-cadherin-RFP and L.m. fluorescence using a 60× 1.4NA Plan Apo oil objective with a z spacing of 0.7 μm.
Image the E-cadherin-RFP with a 561 nm laser at full power for 300 ms exposure.
Image the L.m.-GFP fluorescence with a 488 nm laser at full power for 20 ms exposure.
Acquire brightfield images with a 50 ms exposure.
Scan a line segment or ROI 270 times over a time period of 1 min using a 405 nm laser to achieve a laser wound.
Acquire images every 1 minute for up to 1 hour post-wounding.
Calculate the maximum intensity projections of the E-cadherin-RFP images of the cells overtime.
Perform correlations comparing subsequent frames using the maximum intensity projections.
Run the run_PIV.m script which calls the urapiv.m function to calculate the displacement vectors and store them as .txt files.
Inspect vector displacements using the script readu_laser_ablation.m.
Calculate the mean displacement along the axis of the laser wound.
Construct kymographs showing mean displacement across time and position away from the wound.
Store the mean displacement perpendicular to the wound in the variable “kymographm”.
Plot and save the kymograph in lines 173 to 178 of the readu_laser_ablation.m script.
Calculate the mean uy along the x-axis for each experiment within the first 100 μm from the ablated region.
Calculate the mean uy along the y-axis for each experiment within the first 100 μm from the ablated region.
Prepare the 3 kPa 2-layered polyacrylamide hydrogels on multi-well plates.
Embed fluorescent tracer beads in the upper hydrogel layer.
Coat the upper hydrogel layer with collagen I.
Seed MDCK cells onto the hydrogel-coated surface.
Infect MDCK cells with a low dose of L.m. tagged with mTagRFP.
Place the plate on the stage of an epifluorescence microscope after 4–5 hpi.
Acquire time-lapse images of phase contrast, beads' fluorescence, and L.m. fluorescence.
Analyze the acquired data to calculate 2D traction stresses exerted by infected and uninfected cells during the formation of infection mounds.
Replace the DMEM-based existing medium submerging host cells with 1 mL of live-microscopy medium.
Cover the plate with its lid and place it in the microscope’s environmental chamber equilibrated to 37°C.
Set the microscope up for phase contrast microscopy with a 20× or 40× phase-contrast objective.
Locate a single infection focus using appropriate fluorescence filters.
Ensure host cells around the focus (200–300 μm radius) are not infected.
Adjust the focus to the plane where bead intensity is maximal.
Acquire multi-channel time-lapse images every 10 minutes for 24 hours or more.
Maintain focus to avoid z drift during imaging.
Acquire a reference image of beads at the end of recording.
Add 100 μL of 10% SDS without moving the plate to detach host cells from substrate.
Observe through phase contrast to ensure cell detachment.
Acquire an image of fluorescent beads after removing host cells for reference.
Analyze images using TFM with custom-built scripts in MATLAB.
Determine the 2D deformation of the substrate at each point using a technique similar to particle image velocimetry (PIV).
Compute the local deformation vector by performing a correlation between each experimental image and the unstretched reference image.
Use an interrogation window of 32×32 with an 8 pixel spacing for the correlation analysis.
Calculate the 2D traction stresses that cells exert on the gel as described elsewhere.
Provide the Young’s Modulus (stiffness) of your hydrogel as an input parameter.
Input the finite thickness of the hydrogel measured after manufacturing the hydrogels.
